articleTitle: Enhancing Transmission Efficiency in Vision Transformer Edge Computing via Token Clustering
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Identification, Information and Knowledge in the Internet of Things (IIKI)
abstract: Vision Transformer demonstrates excellent performance, but huge number of parameters hindered deployment. Offloading workloads to the cloud is a promising solution. However, transmission latency and bandwidth limit the efficiency of cloud. Edge computing technology is used to mitigate this problem. Leveraging the computation power of edge devices, data is processed before uploading to reduce transmission latency. Therefore, this paper proposes a clustering-based token subsampling method for the vision transformer partitioning to enhance transmission efficiency. Tokens are encoded based on the cosine similarity clustering result, then all tokens are reconstructed at cloud. Experimental results show that the proposal is effective and can be executed with low latency. For ViT, 23.09% transmitted data is reduced with an accuracy drop of 0.44% within 0.8 ms.

articleTitle: Convolutional Neural Network and Hyperspectral Imaging for Detection of Deoxynivalenol Levels of Barley Kernels
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Identification, Information and Knowledge in the Internet of Things (IIKI)
abstract: Fusarium head blight (FHB) is a devastating disease impacting grain crops worldwide, leading to the production of mycotoxins in grains, with deoxynivalenol (DON) being the most prevalent. DON is present in both unprocessed and processed grains and poses a serious threat to human and animal health. Consequently, barley intended for wheat production, food, or feed must undergo routine testing for DON contamination. The study explored the potential of hyperspectral imaging (HSI) (wavelength range: 382–1030 nm) combined with convolutional neural networks (CNN) to classify DON concentrations in barley grains across various genetic lines. The proposed CNN model achieved 89.41% accuracy in distinguishing barley grains with low DON levels (<5 mg/kg) and high DON content (>5 mg/kg and ≤14 mg/kg). In addition, in the low DON category, 90.08% accuracy was achieved in the identification of Class I with DON ranging from 0.19 mg/kg to 1.25 mg/kg versus Class II DON ranging from 1.25 mg/kg to 5 mg/kg. These findings demonstrate that integrating HSI with CNN offers significant promise for differentiating DON levels in barley grains.

articleTitle: Research and Practice on the Construction of an IoT-based Intelligent Teaching Environment in Universities
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Identification, Information and Knowledge in the Internet of Things (IIKI)
abstract: With the rapid development of information technology and education philosophy, the application of intelligent teaching environments in university education has attracted widespread attention. This research delves into the construction of a multi-type smart classroom environment based on the Internet of Things (IoT) technology, specifically focusing on the application of smart locks and lighting systems in a smart teaching building. The objective is to enhance teaching quality, management efficiency, and student learning experiences. The paper presents a system architecture for an IoT-based intelligent teaching environment and details its pilot implementation at Beijing Foreign Studies University. Based on the system performance analysis in terms of classroom management, security, energy conservation, and teaching effectiveness, the paper also discusses current challenges and future directions for improvement.

articleTitle: YOLO Loss Optimization for Detecting Fruit Defects
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Identification, Information and Knowledge in the Internet of Things (IIKI)
abstract: Japan’s aging population has led to significant labor shortages, particularly in agriculture. An aging workforce and a lack of successors have exacerbated this issue. Additionally, agricultural processes, such as land preparation, seeding, and regular maintenance, require significant manual labor. This further contributes to the labor shortage. To address this issue, process automation through Information Technology (IT) solutions like “factory Automation” have been increasingly adopted in Japan. Automating simple, repetitive tasks can significantly reduce the need for human labor. Among IT solutions, Artificial Intelligence (AI) excels at automating tasks and is widely applied in labor-intensive industries. In this research, we focus on using an Object Detection model, specifically YOLO, to automate the inspection of harvested products for defects. This reduces labor demands in the agricultural sector. This study aims to improve YOLO’s detection accuracy to make it more effective in real-world applications. We propose enhancing the Loss function, a critical component in AI training. Specifically, we improve the L(obj) component, called SBCE, to account for the higher prevalence of small defects compared to larger ones. By scaling the Loss scores for small defects, our model becomes better at detecting small objects. As a result, our improved model demonstrates higher accuracy in object detection. We observe improvements in the mean Average Precision (mAP) of YOLOv7-tiny from 81.51% to 82.13%, as well as increases in Recall (from 68.97% to 72.55%) and mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) (from 52.91% to 53.48%) on the PASCAL VOC dataset.

articleTitle: Real-time Identification of Crop Plant Based on Computer Vision and Crop Signaling Technology for Weed Control
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Identification, Information and Knowledge in the Internet of Things (IIKI)
abstract: Weeding, an important aspects of vegetables growing, requires exact discrimination of crops and weeds which is a major challenge in realizing the process of precision weeding. Crop signaling technology is a novel system approach which could create a machine-readable signal in crops, which are absent in weeds, to distinguish them. Combination of computer vision and color mark sensors (CMSs) was designed to detect the crop plants growing with unique machine-readable plant tags. The effects of different factors (color and area of the plant tags, number of CMSs) on the determination precision was evaluated. In addition, the effects of different concentrations of systematically crop signaling compounds on signal expression (fluorescence intensity, crop vigor, photostability) was explored. The results showed that six CMSs in association with top part of white tags were the optimal configuration for detecting tomato plants. The system effectively detected plant tags and quickly categorized crops and weeds. A one-day treatment to lettuce with 180 ppm compound produced a machine-readable fluorescent signal up to 25 days after transplanting without affecting crop growth. This study provides new insights for accurate identification and localization of crops in weeds.

articleTitle: Evaluating Cloud Assisted Machine Learning for Internet-of-Things Edge Device Security
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Identification, Information and Knowledge in the Internet of Things (IIKI)
abstract: Security solutions based on machine learning enabled Intrusion detection systems (ML-IDS) have been popular for IoT edge device security. The cloud support has been considered to leverage heavy workloads off IoT edge devices such as learning, model fitting and updating. In this paper, we apply ML model optimization techniques as 3 distinct key roles of the cloud layer in Machine Learning as a Service (MaaS) architecture. In order to influence the performance of IoT edge devices, the optimization would require: a) device benchmarking that quantifies the available computing resources and network traffic for the edge device; b) feature weighing that determines the contribution of each extracted feature to the overall ML-IDS operation; and c) dimensionality reduction of important features in the training dataset. We examine feature importance and dimensionality reduction techniques on 3 public IDS datasets and present how they affect ML model performance.

articleTitle: Intelligent Dialogue Method for Educational Applications Based on Improved Large Models
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Identification, Information and Knowledge in the Internet of Things (IIKI)
abstract: This paper designs an improved large model by incorporating a fully connected layer into the pre-trained large model. Furthermore, an intelligent dialogue method for educational applications is devised, leveraging the improved large model to transform user dialogue into structured data demanded by the applications. In the example of the complaints handling application in universities, user complaints are automatically categorized into appropriate consulting units, the effectiveness of this method is validated with an accuracy rate of 93.2%.

articleTitle: Study on a Resnet18-Based Lightweight Recognition ALgorithm of Coal and Gangue
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Identification, Information and Knowledge in the Internet of Things (IIKI)
abstract: The pre-sorting of gangue in raw coal is still predominantly operated manually. The process is characterized by high labour intensity, low efficiency and possible safety risks. A robot designed for the sorting of the gangue in the raw coal is an effective way of completing this task without the need for manual labour. The key technology behind this is the intelligent identification of coal and gangue. The real-time performance has a significant impact on the efficacy of the gangue sorting robot. A multitude of models have been put forth for the recognition of coal and gangue based on machine learning, but remaining several issues, including slow recognition speed and large model size. To address those problem, this paper proposes a recognition algorithm with a backbone feature extraction of ResNet18 for coal and gangue during coal preparation, ResNet18-YOLO. It also studies the feature scale clipping and unstructured pruning of the model with the aim of further improving its recognition speed. Coal and gangue dataset were prepared based on the on-site gangue sorting situation. The investigation results demonstrate that the enhanced ResNet18-YOLO is capable of detecting coal and gangue, and exhibits superior real-time performance, thereby showing an optimum balance between accuracy and real-time detection of coal and gangue. Also commendable is its performance in detecting coal and gangue.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Ensemble Machine Learning Techniques for IoT Edge Device Security
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Identification, Information and Knowledge in the Internet of Things (IIKI)
abstract: Machine learning based Intrusion detection (ML-IDS) has been long enforced for the protection of the IoT against malicious attacks. Researchers focused on improving ensemble intrusion detection methods in order to boost the efficiency of attack detection on resource limited IoT edge devices. However they confined their evaluation platforms to cloud or standalone computing facilities rather than the targeted physical devices. In this paper, we complement our work with feasibility study of managing ensemble-based ML-IDS combiner models on a resourceful physical edge device, and demonstrate the implied limitations of deploying such models in the IoT without cloud support. We also elaborate on the potential of cloud support to support distributed ensemble techniques, resulting in super container models that harness limited resources of IoT edge devices.

articleTitle: User interface design for orientation sensor-based biomechanical feedback in golf
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Identification, Information and Knowledge in the Internet of Things (IIKI)
abstract: This paper presents the development of an intuitive user interface (UI) for a biomechanical feedback (BMF) system to improve the golf swing. The main idea behind the research is to develop an application that will allow golfers to learn correct techniques more efficiently. Our BMF system consists of a mountable device with an Arduino microcontroller and a BNO086 orientation sensor that transmits data at 200 Hz to provide real-time feedback on club orientation. The user interface was developed using the Unity engine to ensure compatibility with different platforms and incorporate semi-realistic graphics to enhance the user’s understanding. By allowing comparisons between excellent and sub-optimal swings of an individual player, it addresses the unique techniques of individual golfers. This focus on individual’s technique is a new approach, that we haven’t found to be used any other research project.

articleTitle: Risk-Averse Trader: A Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Portfolio Optimization Method for Risk-Averse Investors
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Identification, Information and Knowledge in the Internet of Things (IIKI)
abstract: Portfolio management requires continuous adjustments to asset allocation based on market conditions and investor goals, aiming to optimize returns at a given risk level. Risk-averse investors prefer stable returns with lower risk, which poses challenges for standard portfolio management. This paper proposes a deep reinforcement learning-based method, named Risk-Averse Trader, to control investment risk for such investors. We first employ a feature fusion extraction algorithm that combines Multi-scale CNN, U-Net structures, and Multidimensional Attention Mechanisms to enhance the model’s ability to dynamically process financial market data. Additionally, we introduce a downside risk evaluation mechanism specifically designed for risk-averse investors, using the target return as a benchmark to penalize suboptimal daily returns, thereby enhancing risk control capabilities. The proposed model is evaluated on the Dow Jones Industrial Average (2019) and the CSI 300 Index (2023). Results demonstrate improved performance in terms of annualized return, maximum drawdown, and Sharpe ratio, effectively balancing risk and return under varying economic conditions.

articleTitle: Haptic actuators in aquatic environments: an exploratory study
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Identification, Information and Knowledge in the Internet of Things (IIKI)
abstract: The integration of wearable devices into sports and rehabilitation is expanding, particularly in real-time biomechanical feedback (RTBF) applications. This study addresses the challenge of delivering effective RTBF in aquatic environments through haptic feedback. A waterproof wearable device with six vibrotactile actuators, a control circuit, and a microcontroller was developed and evaluated. An exploratory study involving 21 participants (12 males, 9 females) was conducted to assess human perception of haptic feedback. The study examined three independent variables: placement (waist or head), environment (in water or on land), and activity (stationary or in motion). Participants performed eight test scenarios involving 20 distinct haptic patterns. Results indicated that both mounting positions were effective, with differences in recognition rates across conditions and symbol complexities. The findings offer insights into the design and application of haptic RTBF systems in aquatic settings, providing a foundation for future developments in sports and rehabilitation technologies.

articleTitle: Benchmarking Machine Learning based Intrusion Detection for IoT Edge Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Identification, Information and Knowledge in the Internet of Things (IIKI)
abstract: Machine learning-based Intrusion detection (ML-IDS) gained a lot of interest from the research community as security threats facing the IoT are on the rise. Researchers focused on improving intrusion detection efficiency based on machine learning. However, the feasibility of applying proposed ML algorithms to resource limited IoT devices limited. We present a proof of concepts (POC) for ML-IDS for IoT edge device using actual devices. Furthermore, we envisage the lack of virtual environments that mimics the realistic IoT world, puts research completeness on bay. In this paper, we extend the benchmarks of intrusion detection, applied to IoT edge devices of a varying of computing resources. The benchmarks are based on machine learning techniques endorsed by the research community, and adopt popular intrusion datasets for training and testing models. We also utilize the benchmarks to calibrate Virtual-box environment in a novel way to produce virtual machines that closely mimic realistic IoT edge devices. Thus accurate virtualization would become a reliable tool available to researchers to test their approaches.

articleTitle: Attention Distillation for Accuracy Improvement of Vision Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Identification, Information and Knowledge in the Internet of Things (IIKI)
abstract: In recent years, rapid advancements in technology have propelled progress in the fields of image recognition and natural language processing, resulting in the development of numerous applications and services. In particular, the advancement of deep learning has greatly contributed to improving the accuracy of these fields, and the use of AI is becoming more widespread in everyday life [1]. Among them, Vision Transformers (ViT) has emerged as a robust architecture in image recognition. ViT requires a large dataset for training to improve accuracy. To solve this problem, DeiT using knowledge distillation has been proposed. However, this DeiT does not consider each token’s contribution to [CLS] in learning. In this study, a knowledge distillation model training method called ADViT that uses the contribution of each token to Classify token ([CLS]) is proposed. Specifically, the attention map of each token for [CLS] is calculated. In each layer, learning is performed to bring the student model’s attention map closer to the teacher model’s attention map. Then, the accuracy is evaluated, and experimental results show the effectiveness of the proposed method, with accuracy rates of ADViT-Tiny(L1): 98.35%, ADViT-Tiny(L2): 98.06%, ADViT-Small(L1):99.00%, and ADViT-Small(L2): 98.75%, which are higher than those of DeiT, DeiT-Tiny: 96.39%, DeiT-Small: 96.83%. Future work includes managing the number of heads and reducing the computation for more optimization.

articleTitle: Farmland Boundary Extraction Technology Based on UAV Images
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Identification, Information and Knowledge in the Internet of Things (IIKI)
abstract: With the development of 5G and Internet of Things, more and more intelligent agricultural products are put into use, such as solar insecticidal lamps, agricultural robots, intelligent irrigation systems. The efficient operation of these intelligent products deployed in farmland depends on the improvement of ridge information. However, in the existing map system, the gap of ridge information has caused great difficulties in laying these nodes. Because it will be an extremely arduous task to use the traditional method to extract the aerial ridge map, so this paper uses the image processing method to extract the ridge information. To solve this problem, We use the edge detection method to extract the ridge. The main steps include image enhancement, image smoothing and edge detection. In this paper, many experiments have been carried out on these three parts, and the best method has been selected. However, because the traditional edge detection operator can not extract the ridge with high precision, this paper optimizes the edge detection results step by step, so as to obtain an algorithm more suitable for ridge extraction and improve the extraction accuracy. At the same time, in view of the large area of cultivated land, unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) can not get all the images of cultivated land in the case of improving the definition, so it is necessary to stitch the images. Therefore, this paper mainly expounds the basic principles of image stitching based on feature points and image stitching based on regions, and selects an algorithm suitable for stitching farmland images through experimental verification. Finally, through the research of this paper, the vacancy of ridge information can be made up to some extent, and the workload of manual measurement can be reduced.

articleTitle: Short Text Matching Enhanced by Contextual Template for Large Language Models in Data Exchanging Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Identification, Information and Knowledge in the Internet of Things (IIKI)
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in understanding and matching texts of moderate length. However, their performance in short text matching falls short of expectations. This paper proposes a novel approach for LLM-based short text matching, Contextual Template Enhancement (CTE), to improve short text matching accuracy by leveraging contextual information. CTE enhances short texts by incorporating contextual details into templates, transforming short texts into longer texts that better preserve the original semantics while enriching their representational power. Experiments in a data exchanging system show that CTE significantly improves the matching accuracy between short data annotations and data requests.

articleTitle: Weightlifting training assistance system
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Identification, Information and Knowledge in the Internet of Things (IIKI)
abstract: Obtaining an objective information about exercise technique, progress and fatigue management is very important in the sport of weightlifting. This information is usually acquired subjectively by an athlete or a coach. Our motivation is to obtain an objective feedback, in our case physical parameters like vertical acceleration, vertical velocity, height and power produced on the bar by the athlete. We used a wireless sensor device that consists of an orientation sensor, which wirelessly transmits the sensors signals to the user. We performed accuracy tests and validated our sensor device with the professional optical motion capture system from Qualisys. With the validated sensor device, we carried out several measurements of muscle snatch weightlifting exercise. By combining sensors signals and a video recording, we performed an in-depth analysis of the exercise. The results show that the system is functioning as expected and produces the desired results. Using such an assistance system in training helps the coach and the athlete to analyze and evaluate weightlifting technique objectively. The work presented here is used in the development of a standalone weightlifting training assistance system.

articleTitle: Gait Cycle Analysis Algorithm Based on Depth Camera Measurement
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Identification, Information and Knowledge in the Internet of Things (IIKI)
abstract: Gait analysis is widely used in the evaluate in medical gait diagnosis, patient rehabilitation training, and scientific training guidance. Gait analysis system effectively reconstruct 3D human joints model to obtain related gait information through specialized calculations. In this paper, we present a Real-Time Gait Analysis Algorithm (RTGA) based on RGB-D images input, which replaces traditional methods that capturing human body motion trail from wearable inertial measurement units (IMU) equipment. Combining real-time gait data acquisition and a deep learning-based gait medical feature analysis algorithm, we propose a gait measurement and acquisition system based on reliable 3D human joints distribution. We first take joint sequence smooth algorithm to filter the noise data the original 3D motion curve. Then, we perform joints transformation and position correction for the proposed method, which eliminates the gait cycle detection error caused by random noise interference. Finally, we propose a well-designed evaluation system to identify gait cycle and calculate each medical index (such as step width, speed, frequency). We employ Azure-Kinect DK to acquire 3D human body semantic content as input and validate the effectiveness of our RTGA system in the wild.

articleTitle: An efficient neural architecture search based on PCDARTS
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Identification, Information and Knowledge in the Internet of Things (IIKI)
abstract: Deep learning has achieved great achievements in a variety of tasks, such as image classification, speech recognition, and cultural heritage protection. However, manually design deep convolution neural networks for certain tasks requires a long time. Furthermore, it also requires the designer to have certain professional knowledge. Faced with an increasingly complex network architecture, it has become more and more difficult to design only manually. Neural architecture search provides a method to overcome problems in manually designing networks. It mainly includes search space, search strategy, and performance evaluation. In this paper, a new search method, F-PCDARTS, is proposed based on PCDARTS. In the research space, we propose to apply channel shuffle and global context for efficient feature extraction. At the same time, in terms of search strategy, a fixed reduction cell is designed to search normal cells, which solves the difficult and time-consuming problem of search optimization. The experiment results indicate a 9.8% reduction in network search time, requiring only 0.09 GPU days. Furthermore, the validation accuracy of CIFAR10 and CIFAR100 is improved by 0.09% and 0.12%, respectively. The method we propose effectively reduces the time of network search.

articleTitle: Vulnerability of block reorganization on Ethereum 2.0
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Identification, Information and Knowledge in the Internet of Things (IIKI)
abstract: Block reorganization (reorg) may occur when a blockchain fork is deliberately instigated and remains poorly solved on Ethereum. We utilize an agent-based modeling approach to simulate the block generation and decision-making processes of reorg attackers and ordinary validators. We analyze the impact of six validator network structures (i.e., random, regular, small-world, scale-free, hierarchical, and community networks) and four fork selection rules (i.e., LMD GHOST, HLMD GHOST, Goldfish, and RLMD GHOST) on the success rate of reorg attacks. The results show that the community network is more vulnerable to reorg attacks, while the hierarchical network is more resilient to such attacks. In addition, the Goldfish fork-choice rule can significantly reduce the success rate of reorg attacks.

articleTitle: Distributed Learning for Gait-based Human Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Identification, Information and Knowledge in the Internet of Things (IIKI)
abstract: Gait, a biometric characteristic observed during walking, is unique, similar to fingerprints and facial features. Analyzing an individual’s gait pattern enables accurate recognition. Gait recognition technology uses wearable sensors, such as accelerometers and gyroscopes, to collect data from individuals for identification purposes. This study proposes a FedGait method for distributed learning to address privacy concerns in centralized gait recognition. Unlike centralized methods, the proposed approach trains client and global models by sharing model parameters instead of raw data with the central serverensuring privacy during distributed training. This study analyzes both collected gait data and public datasets, allocating the data to local clients based on the number of participants. Experimental results demonstrate that the distributed learning method not only reduces privacy risks but also effectively recognizes gait identity.

articleTitle: Time series classification based on Unet with 2D transformation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Identification, Information and Knowledge in the Internet of Things (IIKI)
abstract: Time series classification has gained significant attention in the data mining field in recent years. Despite the proposal of numerous methods over the past decades, most of these approaches focus on feature extraction in one-dimensional space, which often results in lower classification accuracy. To address this issue, this paper proposes a Time Series Classification method based on U-Net with 2D transformation (TSC-Unet). This method first transforms univariate time series into 2D space and augments the data, effectively enhancing the diversity of the dataset. Subsequently, features are extracted from the 2D space using a fully convolutional network, fully exploiting multi-scale feature information. U-Netwith skip connections, effectively retains and transmits high-resolution features, significantly reducing information loss and improving segmentation performance. Additionally, the ability to learn multi-scale features enables the model to capture details at different levels, thereby enhancing its understanding of complex data. Experimental results demonstrate that TSC-Unet achieves high classification accuracy on the UCR datasets, validating the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Integrating Information Technology in Planning Education: Meeting the Urbanization Challenges of the Information Age
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Identification, Information and Knowledge in the Internet of Things (IIKI)
abstract: As China enters the New-type Urbanization (2021-2035), Big Data in urbanization have posed significant challenges to traditional planning. The requirements of planning talents have transformed along with the information technology applied in planning practices. Planning is an applied discipline which should address urban concerns. This paper aims to provide a vision for future planning education in China in the Information Age and shed insight into the essential competencies required in job markets in the next stage. Taking the Yangtze River Delta as an example, one of the most developed areas in China, by the survey of job posting sites and faculties at target planning schools in this area, this paper examines the supply and demand of planning talents to explore whether current planning education could provide competitive planning talents to meet the urbanization development needs. It is expected that some findings from this study will inform the further evolution of China’s planning education, including designing a curriculum that incorporates data analysis skills, building an urban information knowledge base for systematic qualitative analysis, enhancing computer modelling and simulation in teaching and learning practice, and applying interdisciplinary knowledge to planning practice. Some of these discussions and findings may inform planning education in China and thereby benefit the New-type Urbanization in 2021-2035.

articleTitle: Adaptive Prediction Of Online Learning Based On Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Identification, Information and Knowledge in the Internet of Things (IIKI)
abstract: In recent years, with the advancement of society and the rapid development of internet technology, the popularity of online education has been steadily increasing. Presently, nearly every educational institution worldwide, from elementary schools to universities, has incorporated some level of online teaching. While online instruction offers certain conveniences, it will also be accompanied by the emergence of some problems, given the substantial surge in data related to online learning among students, there is an urgent need for robust data processing methods to forecast their suitability for online education. Previous research underscores the effectiveness of machine learning in tackling diverse data classification tasks. However, there is a scarcity of studies comprehensively comparing various machine learning approaches in the context of online education data. This article utilizes seven distinct, parameter-optimized machine learning approaches to explore a range of performance predictions, spanning both binary and multi-class tasks. During the experimental process, four evaluation metrics and visual aids were employed to assess and compare the methods across these tasks, accompanied by a comprehensive discussion of the experimental results. The results of the experiments reveal that the random forest method demonstrates strong versatility across all selected datasets.

articleTitle: Neighborhood Subgraph-based Illicit Transaction Detection in Cryptocurrency Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Identification, Information and Knowledge in the Internet of Things (IIKI)
abstract: With the widespread adoption of cryptocurrencies, associated illicit activities such as money laundering, fraud, extortion, and Ponzi schemes have garnered significant attention. Traditional studies have extensively employed graph neural network technologies to identify illicit transactions, typically treating the entire transaction network as input to classify its nodes. Although these methods perform well on small-scale networks, they face performance limitations when processing large-scale blockchain transaction data. To address this issue, we propose a neighborhood subgraph-based method for detecting illicit transactions, integrating GCN and LSTM. In this approach, the GCN captures and integrates information from adjacent nodes for each transaction, facilitating a deep understanding of network structures. The LSTM is tasked with capturing the sequence and variations in fund flows, effectively tracking the direction and temporal characteristics of the money flow. Experimental results indicate that when using 3-hop neighborhood subgraphs, our model’s performance surpasses other GCN-based methods. Compared to previous models that require considering the entire transaction network, our approach only needs to utilize information from an average of 80 nodes, significantly improving efficiency.

articleTitle: A New Genre of Content Creation: Combining Mixed Reality Technology and Handicraft
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Identification, Information and Knowledge in the Internet of Things (IIKI)
abstract: This study proposes a new content creation approach that combines mixed reality (MR) technology and handicrafts to foster children’s creativity. We developed a mixed reality platform featuring a real aquarium, where users can create 2D virtual objects by touch on the aquarium’s front glass, which are then automatically transformed into corresponding 3D objects. Additionally, users can materialize these virtual objects through handicrafts or 3D printing, turning them into real, tactile creations. By adding sensor modules, these creations can be further transformed into functional interactive tools. This method encourages creativity and can be applied in various scenarios, such as curriculum learning, science education, and rehabilitation therapy, enhancing children’s creative development.

articleTitle: Innovative Applications of AI and 3D Printing in Digital Dentistry: Enhancing Accuracy and Efficiency in Dental Care
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Identification, Information and Knowledge in the Internet of Things (IIKI)
abstract: Digital dentistry has significantly transformed the way dental professionals deliver patient care by integrating digital technologies into various aspects of the field, such as diagnosis, treatment planning, and restoration. This includes a broad array of technologies like computer-aided design and manufacturing (CAD/CAM), 3D printing, and artificial intelligence (AI), all of which are rapidly advancing and reshaping dental practice. Digital dentistry has ushered in greater precision, accuracy, and efficiency in patient care, leading to improved outcomes. While 3D printing has transformed industries, including dentistry, it still has several drawbacks and limitations. Here are some of the current challenges associated with 3D printing technology: 1) Complex Design Process, 2) Manual Design Adjustments, 3) Limited resolution and occasional inaccuracies in 3D prints, affecting precision in applications. To address these issues, we propose an AI-enabled framework that provides a simplified process to ensure success and minimize human error. Users can quickly import an STL file into the software, select the desired application, and begin printing within seconds. The system automatically analyzes the 3D object, adjusting its orientation and generating supports for splints, crowns, bridges, and surgical guides. In this paper, we analyze the impact of integrating artificial intelligence into the 3D printing workflow for digital dentistry. We focus on how AI can enhance the precision, efficiency, and reliability of dental prosthetics and restorations by automating critical steps that were traditionally manual and prone to errors. Specifically, our proposed framework streamlines the design process by automatically detecting complex geometries, optimizing support structures, and adjusting printing parameters in real time. This AI-enabled approach not only reduces the number of design iterations but also ensures higher resolution and accuracy, overcoming the limitations of conventional 3D printing methods.

articleTitle: Graph Convolutional Neural Network and Attention Mechanism based Emotion Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Identification, Information and Knowledge in the Internet of Things (IIKI)
abstract: Emotion is the subjective cognitive experiences and the corresponding behavioral responses, which plays an important role in interpersonal communication. Emotion classification is an important component of Human Computer Interaction(HCI) that automatically identifies an individual’s emotional state by acquiring physiological or non-physiological signals. Traditional emotion classification methods cannot comprehensively exploit the global and local features contained in EEG signals generated upon stimulation. In this paper, we proposed a graph convolutional neural network and attention mechanism based emotion classification (GCNAEC). First, cross-frequency coupling (CFC) network is leveraged to build adjacency matrices instead of simply combining connections by relative distances and spatial electrode positions of EEG channels. Second, a novel graph attention approach is developed to calculate the attention score of the current graph node and each neighboring node for investigating the differences between single EEG signal and functional connectivity patterns. Third, a novel graph processing method called GAT using PPC is introduced to reduce dimensionality and retain the global information of raw data in each layer. Finally, the experimental results show that the proposed method achieves better performance in emotion classification, in which the classification accuracies are 83.24% for valence dimension and 89.70% for arousal dimension, compared with state-of-the-art methods. In addition, our model outperforms the general GCN model both in terms of recognition accuracy and training time.

articleTitle: Adversarial Attacks on IoT Systems Leveraging Large Language Models
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Identification, Information and Knowledge in the Internet of Things (IIKI)
abstract: Internet of Things (IoT) devices have revolutionized various sectors by providing enhanced connectivity and automated services. However, the integration of these devices into complex networks has introduced significant security challenges. Concurrently, advancements in Language Model (LLM) technologies, exemplified by large-scale models like GPT-4, have given rise to sophisticated cyber-attack strategies. With the widespread use of various large language models, these models may generate a large amount of offensive and socially detrimental content during their use. In response, the primary focus of model developers is to adjust alignment models to prevent the generation of harmful content. Meanwhile, adversarial attackers focus on achieving “jailbreaks” to bypass the alignment measures of model developers, thereby generating harmful content and testing the effectiveness of model alignment. The main attack methods currently include prompt injection, unsafe output handling, denial of service, and general adversarial attacks. We selected the Llama-2-7b large language model as the experimental test model and constructed IoT related issues to achieve the generation of harmful content and desired responses.

articleTitle: A semantic ontology of acupoints in Traditional Chinese Medicine aligning with the Basic Formal Ontology
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Identification, Information and Knowledge in the Internet of Things (IIKI)
abstract: It has been proved that acupoints play important roles in clinical practice. However, due to the less evidence of its anatomical structure, there are few works to explain and understand acupoints from a scientific point of view. In addition, the philosophical connotation in Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) theories and the diversification of various expressions make acupoints full of disputes. This paper aims to establish a refined Acupoint Ontology (AO) based on its attribute description. To improve interoperability with other ontologies, the proposed AO is designed aligning with Basic Formal Ontology (BFO), the recognized upper ontology in the biomedical area. The AO gives formal definitions of core concepts by mapping with terms in BFO. Moreover, the work initially classifies acupoints’ attributes into static and dynamic ones according to TCM theories and biophysics, which gives insights into acupoints in a scientific way. The work is a new and solid step towards a more essential understanding of TCM acupoints and lays a solid foundation for its further standardization and internationalization.

articleTitle: Research on causality extraction algorithm for medical text based on BERT and graph attention network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Identification, Information and Knowledge in the Internet of Things (IIKI)
abstract: This paper proposes the BERT-CGAT algorithm, designed for causality extraction from medical text by integrating BERT with a graph attention network. This approach enhances the accuracy of causality extraction by leveraging BERT’s semantic feature extraction capabilities alongside the relationship modeling advantages of graph neural networks, addressing the complexities inherent in medical texts. The process begins with the construction of a causal graph, followed by fine-tuning the BERT model on medical text to obtain more accurate entity embeddings. Next, a knowledge fusion channel is employed to integrate text encoding information with the causal structure, which is then fed into the graph attention network. Utilizing a multi-head attention mechanism, the BERT-CGAT model processes information from various subspaces in parallel, thereby improving its ability to capture complex semantic relationships within medical texts. A dual-channel decoding layer is designed to synchronize the extraction of entities and inter-entity causal relationships. On a self-constructed diabetes causal entity dataset, the method demonstrates high accuracy and recall rates, validating the effectiveness of the BERT-CGAT model.

articleTitle: Objective quality assessment of generated high-resolution human face images
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Identification, Information and Knowledge in the Internet of Things (IIKI)
abstract: Human face image generation can be used in media, marketing, education, creativity, research and privacy protection. Many deep learning networks have been proposed for generating high-resolution human face images, while the quality of generated human face images are not fully investigated. To bridge this gap, 11 StyleGAN-based networks are firstly trained via the database Flickr-Faces-HQ (FFHQ). Then, each network produces 10,000 high-resolution (1024 × 1024) human face images. After that, the quality of these generated images are evaluated with 6 Face Image Quality Assessment (FIQA) metrics. The average metric values suggest that the generated human face images are with higher quality than the realistic images in the FFHQ database. However, the failure cases of generated images remind us that artifacts and distortions exist, and unreasonable combinations and meaningless contents are produced. Therefore, significant progress is still required for achieving reliable quality assessment and high-accuracy generation of human faces.

articleTitle: Big Data analysis of e-commerce Live Streaming Mode based on Alibaba International Station*
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Identification, Information and Knowledge in the Internet of Things (IIKI)
abstract: In 2020, under the influence of the novel coronavirus epidemic, global cross-border trade has been hindered. The digital transformation of the foreign trade industry has given birth to a new form of cross-border e-commerce live streaming. As a mainstream cross-border e-commerce B2B platform, Alibaba International Station has launched the world’s first B2B cross-border e-commerce live streaming, becoming the focus of attention in the industry. Taking stroller products as an example, this paper conducts SWOT analysis on the cross-border e-commerce live streaming model of Alibaba International Station based on big data and summarizes the path of cross-border ecommerce live streaming to fully empower foreign trade transformation and upgrading in the post-epidemic era.

articleTitle: A clothes warping model based on reference pose map
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Identification, Information and Knowledge in the Internet of Things (IIKI)
abstract: The goal of image visual try-on is to transfer the target garment to the reference photograph and obtain a fitting result. With the popularity of deep learning in recent years, visual try-on has gradually become popular. Current technologies are often dedicated to preserving the texture of the target clothes when distorting it, and preserving as much of the human features as possible in the nontried on parts. However, in most mainstream algorithms at present, when occlusion occurs in the reference image and the posture of the human body changes, it becomes very difficult to warp clothes, fit clothes to human body and preserve the texture. In terms of this issue, we proposed some improved methods and verified them on dataset, which achieved good results. Specifically, pose map of reference human body are added as features when warping the target clothes, so that the model can fully combine the reference human body to warping the target clothes. Furthermore, the structural similarity score is added as the loss function of the clothes warping module, which can reduce the noise, keep the clothes in the same tone before and after warping as much as possible during the warping process. Compared with existing methods, our method can generate try-on images with better perceptual quality and richer details.

articleTitle: The Digital Senses: An Analysis of Internet Use’s Impact on Visual, Auditory, Olfactory, Gustatory, and Tactile Perceptions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Identification, Information and Knowledge in the Internet of Things (IIKI)
abstract: The objective of the study was to examine the correlation between the duration of Internet usage and sensory perception. To this end, the research team developed the Impact of Internet Use on Five Senses (Visual, Auditory, Olfactory, Gustatory, and Tactile) Scale (VAOGTS), a tool designed to assess the relationship between Internet usage and sensory perception. The data were subjected to statistical analysis to ascertain the validity and reliability of the scale. The results demonstrated that the scale is reliable and valid, facilitating further research in this domain. The study revealed that Internet usage significantly impacted the visual and tactile senses, while headphone usage duration affected the auditory senses. Smoking and drinking behaviors facilitated by Internet use indirectly affect gustatory and olfactory senses. Additionally, the study found that watching mukbang or food videos may lead people to experience foods outside of their usual diet, which indirectly affects their sense of gustatory. Overall, this study offers valuable insights into the potential effects of Internet usage on sensory perception.

articleTitle: A Multi-Factor Time Series Forecasting Model for Tax Revenue Based on Hybrid Deep Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Identification, Information and Knowledge in the Internet of Things (IIKI)
abstract: Accurate tax revenue forecasting is essential for formulating sound budgets, optimizing resource allocation, promoting economic growth, and maintaining the stability of public finances. However, numerous influencing factors and complex patterns make tax revenue forecasting a challenging task. In this study, we develop a novel data-driven workflow for forecasting tax revenue in China. Additionally, we construct a multi-factor hybrid deep neural network forecasting model that combines a residual Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network with a Backpropagation (BP) neural network. Furthermore, we investigate five major macroeconomic indicators that affect China’s tax revenue using adaptive lasso: the value added of the tertiary industry, the value added of the industrial sector, the value added of industry as a percentage of GDP, total social fixed asset investment, and the total profit of industrial enterprises above the designated size. These indicators can serve as relevant evidence for further tax analyses. Comparative experiments demonstrate that the proposed LSTM-BP forecasting model yields more accurate tax revenue forecasting results.

articleTitle: Binary Logistic Regression based Intrusion Detection System for CAN bus Security
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Identification, Information and Knowledge in the Internet of Things (IIKI)
abstract: The complex distributed systems installed in vehicles represent the cutting edge of the automotive industry. Electronic control units communicate with each other by sending and receiving messages over a well-known protocol called the Controller Area Network (CAN) bus system. Car Broadcast is a new, but insecure, way to communicate between external electronic devices. However, today’s vehicles are on the brink of security because the CAN network lacks a secure authentication and authorization mechanism. The rise in cyber attacks such as spoofing, spoofing and most commonly denial of service attacks is the result of uncertain measures in the CAN bus network. Although many intrusion detection systems have been developed to provide more secure communication in the vehicle, CAN is still far from being the most secure communication protocol. Since cyber attacks can come from a little-known or completely unknown source, it is essential to take a probabilistic approach based on previous observations from previous attacks. Therefore, we propose a new intrusion detection system that uses binary logistic regression (BLR) to detect and mitigate attacks on a CAN bus network. Binary logistic regression is a very popular predictive model that is widely used in various fields. In binary logistic regression, data is first analyzed, then the probability of individual events is estimated by observing previous data, and then a binary classification model is created. An evaluation of the well-known Nsl-kdd and Kdd-99 datasets shows that our proposed method has a dominant overall performance. The final detection rate is 099.031% using Nsl-kdd with a positive rate as low as 00.073% and the rate of detection is 099.043% using kdd-99 with a positive false rate as low as 00.046%˙ Specifically, to detect denial of service (DoS) attacks, the proposed system achieved a detection rate of 099.061% and 099.098% in Nsl-kdd and kdd-99 dataset respectively. Comparative evaluation confirmed that BLR is more reliable as a memory unit for intrusion detection system.

articleTitle: Privacy-Preserving Blockchain Transactions Synthesis with Diffusion Generative Models
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Identification, Information and Knowledge in the Internet of Things (IIKI)
abstract: Blockchain transactions are increasingly vulnerable to sophisticated attacks, necessitating detection mechanisms that safeguard user privacy. Traditional methods, such as CTGAN and PATE-GAN, often sacrifice privacy to enhance detection accuracy, or compromise detection capabilities to maintain privacy, struggling to effectively balance both. This paper introduces BTGM (Blockchain Transactions Generative Models), an advanced approach that ingeniously combines differential privacy with a two-stage diffusion process, and incorporates Row Modeling based on VGM (Variable Gaussian Mixture) encoding. This hybrid model not only ensures the robust anonymization of transaction data through differential privacy but also effectively learns the distribution of data features via its innovative use of Row Modeling and diffusion processes. Validated on the Elliptic++ dataset, BTGM achieves 0.96 accuracy and 0.86 PRAUC, outperforming SOTA models like CTGAN and STaSy. It effectively thwarts membership inference attacks, maintaining a strong balance between privacy protection and attack detection.

articleTitle: Multi-temporal time window based path optimization for smart recycling bin removal vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Identification, Information and Knowledge in the Internet of Things (IIKI)
abstract: In the context of the digital economy, this study addresses the challenges associated with the scheduling of smart recycling bin emptying vehicles, particularly concerning arbitrary scheduling and high operational costs. A path optimization method is proposed that takes into account multi-time domain constraints within a single recycling cycle. This design leverages the real-time sensing capabilities of Internet of Things (IoT) enabled smart recycling bins. This paper introduces a combination of greedy algorithms, wolf pack algorithms, and variable neighborhood search algorithms to enhance the adaptive crossover, parallel crossover, and mutation processes, a hybrid genetic algorithm, termed the Multi-Temporal Time Window Algorithm (MGA-LTW), is developed. When evaluated against other IGA algorithms on a standardized platform and across various Solomon benchmark scenarios, the MGA-LTW algorithm exhibits a $2.5 \%$ reduction in the average objective value and a $16 \%$ decrease in average computation time. Moreover, the superior performance of the proposed approach is validated through the ablation experiments.In conclusion, the aforementioned method was implemented for optimizing the path of a real intelligent recycling bin reverse logistics clearance vehicle in Jinan. This application resulted in a cost reduction of $26.9 \%$ and a $45.5 \%$ decrease in vehicle utilization. These outcomes highlight the significant practical implications of the method and provide valuable decision-making support for enterprises aiming to enhance management efficiency and reduce operational costs.

articleTitle: A Review of Wearable Gait Recognition: Techniques, Methods, and Future Trends in Biometric Authentication
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Identification, Information and Knowledge in the Internet of Things (IIKI)
abstract: The rapid development of the Internet of Things and smart wearable devices has driven the widespread application of biometric authentication technologies in fields such as healthcare, mobile payment, and smart security. Among these, gait recognition, which relies on dynamic human features, has captured notable attention due to its non-invasive nature and ease of data collection. This paper presents a review of the current wearable gait identification technologies, highlighting key steps such as data acquisition, feature extraction, model training, and recognition testing. The focus is placed on gait feature extraction techniques and associated methods. Moreover, this review explores the use of recognition models, and examines popular gait datasets and their performance across various scenarios. By summarizing recent research developments, we also discuss the challenges and future directions of gait recognition technology, particularly in areas such as data diversity, cross-device adaptability, real-time performance, and data privacy concerns.

articleTitle: Sybil attack simulation on Enhanced IdAPoS protocol with different network topology
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Identification, Information and Knowledge in the Internet of Things (IIKI)
abstract: This study mainly focus on Sybil attacks with the Identity-Augmented Proof-of-Stake (IdAPoS) protocol under different network topologies, including random, scale-free, and hierarchical networks. The study finds that scale-free networks are more resistant to Sybil attacks, delaying their effects. Furthermore, the research improves the IdAPoS protocol by introducing active strategies for honest nodes, which improves the behaviours of this protocol, and by enabling them to dynamically assess and update their trusted and suspicious authority lists based on on-ledger data, which improves the completeness of this protocol.

articleTitle: The Role of VR Serious Games in Emotion Regulation: An Empirical Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Identification, Information and Knowledge in the Internet of Things (IIKI)
abstract: Negative emotions, if left unaddressed under stress, can lead to mental health disorders, making effective emotional catharsis essential for regulation. In recent years, virtual reality (VR) technology has shown promise in emotion regulation. However, the feasibility of using catharsis-based VR serious games for emotion regulation remains underexplored. To address this gap, we developed a VR serious game based on the principles of catharsis therapy, where users experience various scenarios designed to facilitate the release of negative emotions. By integrating behavioral, physiological (EEG), and subjective measures, this study investigates the feasibility and effectiveness of the game in alleviating negative emotions. The experimental findings validate the potential of this VR serious game as a novel therapeutic tool for emotion regulation, offering an effective means of emotional release and contributing to the improvement of overall quality of life.

articleTitle: Detecting Redirected Curvature Gain Thresholds in Vehicle-based VR Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Identification, Information and Knowledge in the Internet of Things (IIKI)
abstract: Recent research has made significant strides in redirecting curvature gain thresholds, primarily focusing on walking scenarios, while vehicle environments have received comparatively little attention. The dynamics of a vehicle impact users’ perceptual capacities in car-based VR experiences, influencing the thresholds for applying curvature gain. This study investigates the redirection of curvature gain thresholds for individuals in vehicles, specifically examining the effects of cognitive styles (field-dependent and field-independent), movement speed, and gain direction on these thresholds. The findings suggest that cognitive styles are important in providing a theoretical framework for the possible use of technology redirection in dynamic, complicated situations.

articleTitle: The Transformer Enhanced Feature Representation with CNNs
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Identification, Information and Knowledge in the Internet of Things (IIKI)
abstract: The self-attention-based Transformer has revolutionized artificial intelligence, achieving remarkable success across various applications beyond traditional convolutional neural networks (CNNs). While multiple studies have explored integrating self-attention mechanisms into CNNs to enhance their performance, these approaches often encounter insufficiency in effectively utilizing self-attention principles. This research proposes a novel approach to address this challenge by integrating the rich and valuable nonlinear information encasulated in the feature maps generated by CNNs with the self-attention mechanisms. Specifically, we leverage the self-attention encoder mechanism to further capture the global dependencies and contextual relations from the informative feature maps, thus enabling more robust and discriminative feature representations. Through experiments and evaluations with benchmark datasets on classification tasks, the findings indicate that our proposed approach not only boosts the performance of CNNs but also delivers a more efficient and scalable solution, achieving the accuracies of 95.65%, 78.48% and 95.65% on datasets CIFAR10/100 and fashion mnist, respectively. This work points to a potential path for future investigations and applications in integrating the transformer encoder with CNNs.

articleTitle: A Survey on the Development and Application of YOLOv5 in the Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Identification, Information and Knowledge in the Internet of Things (IIKI)
abstract: Deep learning plays a growing and crucial role on the Internet of Things (IoT), especially in intelligent data analysis, decision support, and automation control. YOLOv5, as an efficient model for target detection in deep learning, inherits the high-efficiency features of the YOLO series, and significantly improves the performance of real-time detection applications by enhancing the structure of the network and the optimization of the loss function. The article introduces the network structure of YOLOv5 and emphasizes an analysis of its advantages in target detection tasks. Then, the article details the optimization of the network structure based on YOLOv5, including the attention mechanism(CA) and the bidirectional feature pyramid network (BiFPN) structure. In addition, extensions of the evaluation metrics are explored, especially the improved IoU loss functions (e.g., CIoU, EIoU, and SIoU), which address the limitations of the standard IoU loss functions in dealing with targets of different shapes and sizes by introducing new penalty terms. YOLOv5 has been widely used in the IoT domain, and has demonstrated usefulness in the areas of smart city, agricultural monitoring, industrial automation, and environmental monitoring, etc., showing utility and effectiveness, while it has a promising application in the IoT field. By further optimizing the network structure of YOLOv5 and combining it with other AI techniques, it can drive IoT systems towards greater intelligence and automation.

articleTitle: Multi-head Attention Mechanism and Dynamic Semantic Graph Convolution for Facial Action Unit Intensity Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Identification, Information and Knowledge in the Internet of Things (IIKI)
abstract: Facial Action Unit (FAU) intensity estimation can simply rely on subtle responses to facial changes, and thus can be used very flexibly in many domains. Due to the co-occurrence relationship between different FAUs, earlier approaches apply the attention mechanism directly to the entire face image for information extraction, ignoring the connection between global features and local features, which leads to inaccurate FAU localization and cannot flexibly reflect the changes of FAU intensity with respect to subtle face changes. In this paper, a dynamic relationship between global and local features is established between FAUs, based on which a new learning framework is proposed. Specifically, we first capture the intensity, location, and latent features of FAUs in the form of heatmap regression, and then divide the task into two branches. The first task branch leverages an attention mechanism combined with FAU position and intensity heatmaps to extract global features. The second task branch models the activation states of FAUs within latent features, enabling dynamic exploration of correlations among AU local features. These global and local features are then interactively fused to predict AU intensity levels. The proposed method’s effectiveness is validated through experiments on the DISFA and BP4D benchmark datasets, showing superior performance compared to existing approaches.
